video_title: NBA On NBC Family Roundtable: Melo, Reggie & Jamal Talk Hoops

quotes.speaker: Reggie Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: Reggie Miller on Vince Carter's unique physical and skill set
quotes.excerpt: The ability to do small man things in a big man body.
quotes.quote: The ability to do small man things in a big man body. You can come off the bench and score better than anybody. Anybody I want to make a shot, big moment, you.

quotes.speaker: Jamal Crawford
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamal Crawford on why Reggie Miller was the toughest to guard
quotes.excerpt: I think for me personally, it would have been Reggie.
quotes.quote: I think for me personally, it would have been Reggie. I remember when he was 38, 39, last year, and I was with the Knicks, and he was still moving. I'm like, switch, switch somebody, anybody.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady on the physical toll of guarding Carmelo Anthony
quotes.excerpt: Your body hurts after playing against him.
quotes.quote: I'm going to go with Melo because I competed with him in the West, and I mean, you hear people talking about him all the time. It's like, your body hurts after playing against him. Because he, when you in the trenches with him, it's bully ball. Like, his physicality, like, it's like you in the trenches like two linemen going at each other every fucking play. And that hurts, man. And then, you know what I'm saying, that takes a lot, that takes a lot because now you got to go on the other end, you got to score now, you know what I mean? So, going up against that for 40 minutes a night, you know, that, that's tough.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony on the difficulty of guarding Vince Carter
quotes.excerpt: With Vince, it was more you had to make sure your footwork was correct.
quotes.quote: With Vince, it was more you had to make sure your footwork was correct. And you, you cannot jump. If you jump, or if you reach, yeah, I teach. That's it. Yeah.

quotes.speaker: Reggie Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: Reggie Miller on the challenge of guarding Carmelo Anthony
quotes.excerpt: Having to guard Reggie is like, it was a master class of patience.
quotes.quote: Having to guard Reggie is like, it was a master class of patience, but knowing the ins and outs of the game and how to maneuver through your teammates. Like, you were so good at, even if, yo, you, your start and stop was so good, you just needed the quick bump to get an advantage. And if you caught up, you would slow down again or you were so good at pulling Rick Smits or any big, like the Davis boys, or the Davis boys in your line of path, yes, before that was illegal. When it was legal, which what made them so hard to guard because once he saw a window, it went up.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady on the discipline required to guard Reggie Miller
quotes.excerpt: How he plays and running off screens is predicated on you being disciplined.
quotes.quote: How he plays and running off screens is predicated on you being disciplined. The minute that you try to shortcut and cheat, like you're dead. And like he said, like you running through these Davis boys, bro, they screens, they screens. They screening. Reggie Miller was the one person that it felt like it was taking away your offense.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony on the difficulty of guarding Reggie Miller
quotes.excerpt: I guarded Reggie one year, and I was just looking down, I ain't no way I'm chasing him.
quotes.quote: I guarded Reggie one year, and I was just looking down, I ain't no way I'm chasing him. I'm not switching off. Right. But y'all had, y'all didn't have the switch aspect that they have today. Right, right, right. Right. So, if he got you, and you was one step behind, you're done. Because no bigs know how to hedge out and get back to their big, right. So to me, that was special to watch.

quotes.speaker: Reggie Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: Reggie Miller on his ability to manipulate referees
quotes.excerpt: And the last aspect to that, you are a master manipulator. You knew how to manipulate the foul.
quotes.quote: And the last aspect to that, you are a master manipulator. You knew how to manipulate the foul. The refs, me. Because of his shot motion, he was able to, you know, where you like, I didn't foul him. But he knew how to manipulate it to where it looked that way.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady on the difficulty of guarding Carmelo Anthony
quotes.excerpt: When I would run floppy against him, I was like, I'm trying to get to the basket.
quotes.quote: When I would run floppy against him, I was like, I'm trying to get to the basket because that's my advantage. Okay, I'm going to say this about you, and they can pull up the footage later, but there was a game in Indiana, right, and this is one of our best teams, but we had Chris Mullin trying to guard you, maybe Jalen Rose, and you were on the wing, and I was on the weak side, when you went baseline, and you went with the boom, and I made a business decision. Get out the way. That was a dunk hard around the world. I am not getting in this holster. You already knew. I already knew. When he went, when he took that first step, I think it was on Mullin, I was like, nope.

quotes.speaker: Reggie Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: Reggie Miller on the evolution of player skills
quotes.excerpt: They had footwork and athleticism. So you either had one or the other. Mike was different.
quotes.quote: Look, I didn't have athleticism. So they had footwork and athleticism. So you either had one or the other. Mike was different. He had them both. So you saw the evolution of how they, it was only Mike, and maybe Kobe, and then Kobe and the, then it was them with footwork. They could beat you with their footwork, they could beat you with their shoulder work, they could post up, they could shoot over you, and then they could dunk over you.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony on the evolution of player skill sets
quotes.excerpt: Today you're not intentional on a specific skill set. You're intentional on coming off a pick.
quotes.quote: Today you're not intentional on a specific skill set. You're intentional on coming off a pick in the workout. You're intentional on trail threes, you're intentional, you know, you intentional on same leg, same hand on the layups. Those are the things you're intentional. You're not working on like coming off a pin down curls 100 times in the workout. You're not one dribble pull up, you know, working on one dribble pull ups 200 shots in the workout left, then you go 200 shots on the right. You're not working that intentionally.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady on the importance of footwork and creating space
quotes.excerpt: She wants to play more like around the free throw line and in the mid post.
quotes.quote: I was just at girls ABCD in Oakland, and one of the players, Alia Edwards, plays in the WNBA. She, that's what she wanted to learn. She was like, I want to play more like around the free throw line and in the mid post. I was like, how's your footwork? She's like, that's what I want to work on this summer. I was like, man. So that team is moving to Houston, right? And I live in Houston. I was like, yo, come to my house, I'm going to work with you on that. Because I was telling her, I was like, you don't need a lot of dribbles. Like in this area you trying to play, three max. You just need to know how to create space. And that's what I was so good at, right? I learned how to create space, and then when that space is created, the ball has to go up. I'm not over dribbling, I'm not overthinking. When I create space to get my shot up, because I'm confident, any shot is comfortable to me. So when that space is created and I can get my shot, it's going up.

quotes.speaker: Reggie Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: Reggie Miller on the essential traits of an effective iso player
quotes.excerpt: You've got to be able to create your own shot within one, two, or three dribbles max.
quotes.quote: To me, you've got to be able to two things. Be able to create your own shot within one, two, or three, three dribbles max. And you've got to be able to score with contact. Yes. Minimal or a lot. You've got to be able to score with contact because you might be off balance, right? So either creating contact and you get your shot off clean, or creating contact and then letting them recover and then they they bump and then you finish and one.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady on creating an advantage in 1-on-1 situations
quotes.excerpt: How quickly can you create the advantage? And then from there you do what you do.
quotes.quote: For me, I think how quickly can you create the advantage? And then from there you do what you do. Like for all of us, when you, when you have the advantage on a player, I think we all do something different. You get to the bump to create your advantage, you get to the handle, quickness, what a ball fake, first step, whatever it is, I feel like the quicker, because I feel like if you're playing, you have three dribbles, you play with, you give the defender the chance. But how quickly can you create the advantage to get to, fade, lane, whatever.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony on the importance of angles in isolation scoring
quotes.excerpt: Mines is I always was an angle guy. So I needed an angle.
quotes.quote: Mines is I always was an angle guy. So I needed an angle. And and if I got that angle on you, and you wasn't getting back in front of me. So if you tried to get back in front of me, then I'm utilizing the spin, I could utilize a step back. How did you initially create that angle though? Was it a jab? Was it a ball fake? Mines was a jab. It was nasty. But I also, people think I, people always say I, I, I played with the ball back there, right? What are you talking about? It's, it's, it's because if I just catch it in triple threat, like you got time to set your feet and, but if I put the ball right here, you got to think about how you going to angle, right? And if I bring it down, now you really got to make a decision. And the minute that you decide to just open up, I'm going.

quotes.speaker: Reggie Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: The New York Knicks championship run was a perfect storm
quotes.excerpt: It was a perfect storm of them playing well at the right time.
quotes.quote: It was a perfect storm of them playing well at the right time. And if you go back and look at each game and all five finals game, every player on this Knicks team had a role in the championship. Alverado was huge in game four the comeback. Deuce McBride was huge knocking down threes in the Atlanta series. Everyone had a role to play. Obviously you have the closer, the Derrick Jeter, and Jalen Brunson and all that, but it was a perfect storm of them playing well at the right time. And then obviously Karl-Anthony Towns reinventing himself as being a point center. He took less for them to win more which was the chip. A perfect storm for them to win.

quotes.speaker: Reggie Miller
quotes.summary_phrase: Reggie Miller addresses his complicated relationship with Knicks fans
quotes.excerpt: I will never ever. I love when players get the ultimate goal.
quotes.quote: I will never ever. I love when players get the ultimate goal. I love the organization. This has I am so happy for Patrick Ewing and John Starks and all. You know how many battles I had with these dudes, right? And for them to be rewarded, seeing their faces, that is great for me. I just don't like hearing it from Knicks fans that I hate on them. I don't hate. Some of y'all can be idiots, that was on full display, too, in the playoffs.
